column1: What is a flow chart?
column2: A diagram that shows the sequence of steps and decisions in a process.

column1: What is the main purpose of a flow chart in media?
column2: To plan how an interactive product works – its navigation, user journeys and logic – before it is built.

column1: Which flow chart symbol marks the start and end?
column2: The terminator – a rounded rectangle or oval.

column1: What does a rectangle represent in a flow chart?
column2: A process – an action or task to be carried out.

column1: What shape is the decision symbol?
column2: A diamond.

column1: What should be written inside a decision symbol?
column2: A question, such as "Password correct?"

column1: How should the exits from a decision symbol be labelled?
column2: With each possible answer, usually Yes and No.

column1: What does a parallelogram represent in a flow chart?
column2: Input or output – data entered by or shown to the user.

column1: What do the arrows (flow lines) show?
column2: The direction of flow from one step to the next.

column1: In which directions should a flow chart normally be read?
column2: Top to bottom or left to right.

column1: How many start points should a flow chart have?
column2: One.

column1: What is a 'dead end' in a flow chart?
column2: A route that stops without reaching an end or another step – a sign the chart is incomplete.

column1: Name three media products that are planned with flow charts.
column2: Any three from: websites, apps, video games, interactive quizzes, e-learning, kiosks, DVD menus.

column1: Why do web developers use flow charts?
column2: To plan site navigation and how pages link together so users never reach a dead end.

column1: How do game designers and programmers use flow charts?
column2: To plan branching choices, levels and the logic for characters.

column1: Why might a client look at a flow chart?
column2: To check and approve how the finished interactive product will work before it is built.

column1: Give a non-interactive use of a flow chart in the media industry.
column2: Setting out a process, such as an emergency procedure in a TV studio.

column1: Name two items of hardware used to create a hand-drawn flow chart.
column2: Any two from: paper, pens or pencils, a ruler or template, a whiteboard.

column1: Name two types of software that can be used to create a flow chart.
column2: Dedicated diagramming software (e.g. Visio, Lucidchart, draw.io) or the shape tools in word processing, presentation or DTP software.

column1: Give one advantage of creating a flow chart digitally.
column2: It is easy to edit, rearrange and share, and the shapes are neat and standard.

column1: Give one advantage of a hand-drawn flow chart.
column2: It is quick for early ideas, needs no software and is good for group brainstorming.

column1: When is a flow chart appropriate to use?
column2: When a product has choices, branches or logic – what happens next depends on the user.

column1: Why is a flow chart less suitable for planning a poster?
column2: A poster is static with no choices or sequence – a visualisation diagram is better.

column1: What is the difference between a flow chart and a wireframe?
column2: A flow chart shows how a product works (the routes and logic); a wireframe shows what each screen looks like (the layout).

column1: Give two features of an effective flow chart.
column2: Any two from: standard symbols, complete routes with no dead ends, short clear labels, a logical direction, few crossing lines, matches the client brief.

column1: A question has been drawn in a rectangle. How should it be improved?
column2: Redraw it as a diamond (decision symbol) with labelled exits for each answer.

column1: A "Password correct?" decision only has a Yes route. What is missing?
column2: A No route – for example show an error message and let the user try again.

column1: How can a key improve a flow chart?
column2: It helps users who do not know the symbols (such as the client) to understand the chart.

column1: What is a 'loop' in a flow chart?
column2: A route that goes back to an earlier step – e.g. returning to a question after a wrong answer.

column1: In which part of R093 are flow charts covered?
column2: Topic Area 3.3 – documents used to design and plan media products.
